audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it directly: LeBlanc wins 45.73% over 2751 games but the content chart handed LeBlanc 6 of 7 stages, while the full layer read 'Skill' on every row — two layers disagreeing, and both at odds with the data.
audit.why: LeBlanc genuinely owns levels 1-2 (ranged sigil poke against a melee with only an 8s Crescent Strike). From 3 Lunar Rush is online, from 6 Moonfall starts the fight for Diana, and from one item her sustain lives through a rotation. A sub-46% matchup cannot be six LeBlanc rows.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-1 LeBlanc, rows 2-3 Skill, rows 4-6 Diana, proposed as one atomic group with every full/content pair matched and every why rewritten to agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] said Diana has 'no mobility before 6' and spikes[1] called Moonfall 'her only real engage tool pre-6' — the two contradict each other and both are wrong.
audit.why: Lunar Rush is a basic ability, 22/20/18/16/14, available from level 3, and it has NO cooldown when used onto a target afflicted with Moonlight by Crescent Strike. That reset is her engage, not the ultimate.
audit.corrected: Spikes re-keyed: Lunar Rush from 3 as the engage, Moonfall at 6 as the 100s fight-starter, first item as the sustain flip.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was stated only as 'Moonlight marks reset her dash'; the page also told you to 'dash in with your own E' and credited the shield to her passive.
audit.why: LeBlanc's dash is Distortion (W, 15s at rank 1). Diana's shield is Pale Cascade (W, 15/13.5/12/10.5/9), not Moonsilver Blade — the passive is the every-third-hit cleave plus attack speed after a cast. The load-bearing fact for LeBlanc is that Lunar Rush cannot reach her at all unless Crescent Strike has landed first, so dodging the arc removes the entire engage.
audit.corrected: Dash named as W; the shield attributed to Pale Cascade with its cooldown; the Crescent-Strike-gates-Lunar-Rush condition stated in early, spikes and cooldowns.

audit.why: Crescent Strike 8s->6s, Lunar Rush 22s->14s and Moonfall 100s->80s are the clocks that decide when you may step forward.

audit.whatIsWrong: Eleven misgendered fields (Diana called he/his) plus two copy-paste bleeds; mid text called Moonfall a 'pull/root'.
audit.why: Lint findings are deterministic; Moonfall's kit text says draws in and slows, with no root.
audit.corrected: All pronouns corrected, both bleeds replaced with title-matching bodies, Moonfall described as a pull and slow.

edits.before: Diana's kit before 6 is just a skillshot and a shield — if you play around her Q cooldown, you get a clean E-dash trade every time it's down since she has zero other way to close distance or escape. Her passive moonlight procs do add up over multiple trades though, so don't get greedy chain-trading; look for a hard all-in the moment her Q whiffs rather than a slow poke war. This is your best window to build a lead before her ultimate comes online.
edits.after: Diana before 6 is Crescent Strike on 8s, a 15s Pale Cascade shield, and Lunar Rush from level 3 — and Lunar Rush only reaches you if Crescent Strike marked you first, so the arc is the whole fight. Dodge it and you get a clean W trade with nothing she can do about it; her Moonsilver Blade third hit adds up, so don't chain-trade at her range. Build the whole lead in this window, before Moonfall comes online at 6.

edits.before: At 6 she gains Moonfall, a pull/root that lets her force an engage onto you or peel for allies — this is the point the matchup starts to even out. Your burst combo still kills her if you catch her Q down, but she can now punish you back with a full R-Q-W-AA rotation if she lands the pull first. Play a bit more cautious around her all-in windows here rather than freely diving.
edits.after: At 6 she gains Moonfall, a 100s pull and slow that lets her force an engage onto you or peel for allies — this is the point the matchup turns over to her. Your burst still kills her if you catch Crescent Strike down, but she punishes back with a full R-Q-W rotation the moment the pull lands. Play around her all-in windows here rather than diving freely.

edits.before: This is where Diana genuinely takes over — a completed Riftmaker gives her sustained true damage and tankiness that lets her survive your burst and kill you back through the fight, and her ultimate becomes a teamfight-defining engage/reset tool with the passive orbit-shield absorbing your poke. You want this game over before her second item; if it drags, you have to play from range and avoid ever getting pulled into her orbit.
edits.after: This is where Diana genuinely takes over — a completed Riftmaker gives her sustained true damage and tankiness that lets her survive your burst and kill you back through the fight, and her ultimate becomes a teamfight-defining engage with Pale Cascade, 9s at rank 5, absorbing your poke on top. You want this game over before her second item; if it drags, play from range and never stand inside Moonfall's 475.

notes: CHART REBUILT AS ONE GROUP. On disk the full layer read 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[] read LeBlanc x6 + Diana — a live cross-layer disagreement, and the packet itself flags the chart as contradicting a 45.73% win rate. New chart: rows 0-1 LeBlanc (ranged poke vs a melee with only an 8s Crescent Strike), rows 2-3 Skill (Lunar Rush online at 3), rows 4-6 Diana (Moonfall, then sustain). Every row that moves has both layers edited and its why rewritten in this same proposal; rows 0-1 and 6 needed no content edit because win[] already held the target value. Biggest factual error killed: 'Diana has no mobility before 6' and 'Moonfall is her only real engage pre-6' — Lunar Rush is a level-3 basic ability that has NO cooldown into a Moonlight-marked target.
